# Phillips

## Overview

- **Age:** Adult
- **Gender:** Male
- **Status:** Alive
- **Role:** Schoolteacher
- **Nicknames:** Mr. Phillips

## Appearance

Mr. Phillips is described as an unremarkable man in physical appearance. He often wears a somewhat worn suit while teaching. He frequently carries a chalk-dusted look and holds himself with an air of mild condescension.

## Personality

Mr. Phillips is a sarcastic, inefficient, and incompetent schoolteacher who lacks empathy and enthusiasm for his profession. He practices blatant favoritism toward certain students while picking on others, particularly Anne Shirley. He is often lazy, spending class time writing love letters rather than instructing his pupils. His lack of discipline and fairness renders him deeply unpopular among most of the Avonlea school children.

## Traits

- Incompetent
- Sarcastic
- Partial and unfair
- Lazy

## Abilities

- Teaching (poorly)

## Goals

- Court Prissy Andrews while doing as little teaching work as possible

## History

Mr. Phillips serves as the schoolmaster at Avonlea when Anne Shirley first attends school. On Anne's first day, he severely humbles and embarrasses her by misspelling her name on the blackboard and forcing her to sit next to Gilbert Blythe as punishment for being late. His harsh and public punishments lead Anne to refuse to attend school for several months. Throughout his tenure, he openly woos one of his oldest students, Prissy Andrews, paying far more attention to her than to his instructional duties. At the end of his school term, he leaves Avonlea, much to the relief of most of his students.

## Background by volume

- Hired as the schoolmaster for the Avonlea school prior to Anne Shirley's arrival.

## Affiliations

- Avonlea School — Schoolmaster

## Relationships

### Anne Shirley

- Enemy of — Unfairly targeted and antagonized her in school

### Prissy Andrews

- Romantic with — Courtet her while she was his pupil
